chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Joe Glaser on the road and two quarts of whiskey at the Club Panama
summary: Glaser rode the bus the first year and told clubs to give the band anything; in Chicago Holmes took him at his word and got sick.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, did Glaser go on the trips? Or did he stay...

No. He would come around. The first year he went out with us. The first year, he was in the bus with us. He was a forty-year-old manager, you know; he was forty during them days. He was good in this kind of way. We'd be in place where we couldn't get served, and he would, like, get out of the bus and he'd go and come back with all kind of food and stuff, and give it to us -- you know, come in the bus with it.

And then, like, we'd be playing a dance at night, and there would be a...we were gonna lay over or something, and there's a nightclub or something around there that had shows in the back, an (?)all-farmers'(?) club, out to have a little sport, see what's going on. Well, we fallen in the club, and some of these guys, they pick up their chicks or something, one of them things, you know, and be in the ..(?).. Joe Glaser would fall in the club: "Any of my boys in here from the Louis Armstrong band, give 'em anything they want." Oh, he liked that. He was loud, you know.

So we hit Chicago, and I was in a nightclub up there -- I think my wife had just come to see me. And Joe was up there, and he come in the club -- the Club Panama we was in. He says, "Give my boys anything they want." So I told the waiter, "Give me two quarts of whiskey." And my wife and I had two quarts. I just did that because he said, "Give them anything they want." I said, "if he won't pay me nothin', I'll get it some kind of way." So he put the whiskey on the table, and I sat there and drank as much as I could. I got sick as a dog. I was sick as a dog. Last thing I remembered was, I was outside the club with my arm wrapped around a lamppost -- I'm tryin' to hold myself up.
That was when I was just starting to drink. I didn't go for drinkin'. But every once in a while, I run across an occasion like that, and I'd have to take advantage of it.
